items: Removal Trap: Remember that the Governor appoints SHRC members, but ONLY the President has the authority to remove them.
Limitation Period: Questions frequently test the 1-year limitation clause for taking up cases of human rights violations.
Overlapping Jurisdiction: NHRC cannot inquire into a matter already being investigated by an SHRC or another statutory commission.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both NHRC and SHRC derive their powers from the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (amended in 2019).
NHRC members are appointed by the President, whereas SHRC members are appointed by the Governor of the respective state.
Members of SHRC can be removed ONLY by the President, not the Governor, ensuring independence of office.
Both commissions function as advisory bodies with powers of a civil court but lack punitive authority.
Neither commission can inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.
